findings: The original Kenney Mini Market 1.0 CC0 models and creator/additional credits are retained. The three inspected shelf models have no animation clips; pack-wide feature counts do not apply to these static assets.

The selected crop emphasizes one horizontal support surface holding two existing source boxes, with the frame and backing identifying the shelf context. The lower shelf and feet are intentionally outside the crop; the backing is cut horizontally below the selected surface.

Six carton nodes and two rear box nodes are hidden at scene level. Frame/visible-box geometry, material, texture and per-node transforms are preserved; camera, lighting, root recentering and documented crop/resize produce the image. No replacement object geometry is introduced.

The shelf front edge and supporting frame remain distinguishable at actual Match 126x72 and Memory 144x74 sizes, including matched opacity and real badge. Clean source coloring fits the accepted cart, basket and pallet family.

adaptations: Rendered the acquired Kenney Mini Market 1.0 shelf-boxes GLB with its original colormap. Frame and visible box geometry, materials, textures and per-node transforms are preserved; only the model root is recentered.
Six source carton nodes and two rear box nodes are hidden at scene level, leaving the source frame and its two front upper boxes. No replacement geometry or added text/target label is used.

Camera and studio lighting emphasize one upper support surface. A 768 by 768 transparent render is cropped to focus rectangle [0,0,768,640], then alpha bounds plus a 16-pixel margin and Lanczos resizing produce 512 by 309. The crop deliberately cuts the backing panel below the selected shelf and excludes the lower shelf and feet.

Root inspected eight original source views, four sparse compositions, and actual Match 126 by 72 and Memory 144 by 74 cards in unmatched/matched states. The support edge remains distinguishable with the real badge and matched alpha. This is scoped AI image review, not a participant recognition study or domain/module approval.
